What I already told you yesterday or the day before is that sometime in the month of July or August, the only person I spoke to was the Deputy Minister of Justice and General Administration, and that was about the functioning of the courts. That was either in July or August 1992, either the end of July or the beginning of August. I testified about that, I provided my testimony to that effect, but I'm not familiar with any other delegation that arrived in order to implement anything. This is the third time you're asking me, and I don't know whether my answer satisfies you, but I can't tell you anything more than I actually knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm satisfied. I just want to make a clear record of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, if we look at document P 01161 -- P 01661.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We see these are minutes of the 30th session of the HVO, and you indicated that you were familiar with the decree that we talked of. I don't see your name in the minutes, but first let me ask you: Have you had an opportunity to review these minutes, and do you recognise or can you confirm to us, one way or the other, that you would have been aware of the discussions in this particular session as a result of your position in the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that because of the following session of the HVO, these minutes were adopted. I was not at this session. I delegated my deputy, Karlo Sesar, to attend the session. But knowing how the HVO function, I know that the minutes of the previous sessions are adopted at the following sessions. So I had an opportunity to read the minutes, and my deputy also informed me and reported to me about the discussions that were held at this particular session that I didn't attend.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Two very quick points. If we look at item 2, under item 2, it is said that, and I'm reading in the middle of the paragraph, that: "A special social and political communities which should function during a state of war is neither envisaged by the current Constitution of the Republic of BH, nor is it in line with the Vance-Owen Peace Plan or the agreements signed by the Muslim and Croat delegations in their talks in New York." Then I'll skip a paragraph, I'll skip the next paragraph, and then it goes on to say: "In addition to being illegitimate and unacceptable, the decision on districts is also impossible to implement. For instance, the district of Mostar includes, according to the decision, the municipality of Bileca, Gacko, Ljubinje, Nevesinje, Trebinje, which have wholly been occupied by the aggressor for almost a year now. On the other hand, it is obvious from the list of powers and duties of the district administrative bodies that BH is being divided as a unitary basis, which is the aim of strengthening the central government of the republic. This is a concept similar to the former Yugoslavia, just in another form." And then it goes on, at the very beginning of the next paragraph, it says: "The decision on the establishment of the so-called districts of Mostar and Livno obviously ignores the existence of the HVO HZ-HB." And my first question is: Do you agree with what is being stated here in these minutes? Now, you told us or we already heard from you that it's not constitutional, and we'll provide the additional information for Judge Prandler and others. You told us that this was not in compliance with the Vance-Owen Peace Plan that you were involved in, and we'll see concretely in a second. But do you agree with the part where it says "impossible to implement because these areas are under Serb occupation," and, number 2, that this seems to be another way of diluting the Croatian people's constitutive powers in establishing a unitary state?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that I've already partly provided my opinion about that. It is correct that the territorial organisation of the districts by and large operates from the Vance-Owen Plan that had been adopted by the Bosniak and the Croat side. It is true that Gacko, Ljubinje, Trebinje, Nevesinje, Bileca became a part of the District of Mostar, although they were under Serb occupation; and, realistically, it was not possible to include them into this district. It is also true that the establishment of these districts, as may be seen from the previous documents, was requested through the commanders of the BiH Army, i.e., the 4th Corps, which is very indicative and very characteristic. It is true that all of this was happening at a time when attempts were made to implement the Vance-Owen Plan. In my opinion, all of this was nothing but an obstruction to the implementation of the Vance-Owen Plan, even by force if necessary through the BH Army, i.e., through the 4th Corps, when it came concretely to the issue of Mostar. And I believe that after this session which was held at the time, the HVO sent a letter to the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina in which they expressed a position very similar to the one I provided just now and that I provided earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if we look at the letter that you mentioned, or if we look at document 1D 01972, we see that it is signed by Dr. Jadranko Prlic on behalf of the HVO, dealing specifically on the formation of Mostar and Livno districts. Is this what you were referring to about the letter that was sent to the government, which is also based on the minutes of the meeting that we saw earlier in P 01661?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I took part in the drafting of this document that was signed by Dr. Jadranko Prlic, president of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We do note, we do note that on item 4, page 2, it makes reference to, it says here: "The formation of Mostar and Livno districts has not been regulated either by the current Constitution of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which was signed by both Muslim and Croatian delegations at the peace negotiations in Geneva and New York." And can we conclude from this that you're talking about the Vance-Owen Peace Plan?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. It's about the Vance-Owen Plan, and it notes that the establishment of this district is neither in conformity with the Constitution of Bosnia and Herzegovina or with the already accepted and signed Vance-Owen Plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we look at P 09276. This was a map that was provided, I believe, by the Prosecution. It's map 11. I don't know if we're able to pull it up in the e-court. And while that's being done, if I could have the assistance of the usher to put something on the ELMO. I don't know if that's possible to do both at the same time. If not, I could do it one at a time. And on the ELMO, I guess we will need some sort of IC number for this document, this map. What is on the ELMO is not on the e-court. And, Your Honours, it may be of some assistance to you if you go back to the decree itself and you look under Article 6 of item 4. It talks about the District of Mostar, and it lays out -- I apologise. I apologise, Your Honours. If you look at the bottom, at the very end, there's a decree with the power amending, so that would be the second-to-last page of this document, Your Honours. It's attached to the decree. This is the amending of it. Again, under item 4, it says: "District of Mostar, Centre in Mostar, for the territories of the municipalities of Bileca, Capljina, Cikluk, Gacko, Grude, Jablanice, Konjic, Siroki Brijeg, Ljubinje, Ljubuski, Mostar, Neum, Nevesinje, Posusje, Stolac, and Trebinje." My apologies to my colleagues for my pronunciation of the names, but that's the best I can do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we look at what was envisaged in the district for Mostar, and if we now compare this with map 11 of P 09276, and we can provide this to you, sir. Do you have it? Okay. Now, can you please tell us whether Mostar District comports with the Vance-Owen Peace Plan that was being negotiated at that very moment, where Izetbegovic and company were signing and agreeing, while at the same time pushing the military to establish a district of this sort which, as you said now and back then with your colleagues, was unconstitutional?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to thank you because I believe these maps confirm what I've already said; namely, that there are significant - not small, significant - departures in the structure of the district from the agreed and initialled Vance-Owen Plan. If we look at these maps, specifically the District of Mostar, we will see that municipalities Gacko, Nevesinje, Bileca, Ljubinje, and Trebinje, under the Vance-Owen Plan belong to a Serb province or a province with a majority Serb population; whereas, these same municipalities, in the establishment of districts, were included in Mostar District. I believe this one example of the Mostar District is sufficient; although, I could also speak of District Livno where, with the use of the BH Army and its security services, security services being attached to the services in Mostar, Livno, they wanted to belong to Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: For the Judges, I'm going to eat up some of my time, and I don't mind. It's like being in, I guess, a casino, where you have so many chips to play.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So let's put Livno on just to show you. Again, it's worth showing because we see Livno; and from your answers, it would appear that a double policy or some nefarious attitudes are being displayed by the negotiators?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Objection to the state of counsel, again, characterizing the evidence. It's for the witness to testify, and for the Trial Chamber to draw its conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm only trying to help the Trial Chamber, Your Honour, but I take his point.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not clearly visible on the map whether it is, indeed, so. I can't read the text, but I believe this is Glamoc, which according to the Vance-Owen Plan was included in a province with a majority Serb population. Here, it is included in Livno District.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. If you look at -- if you look back at document 1D 00509, and you look at the amended redistricting, if you want to call it that, under number 10, you see there Livno, with the centre of Livno, the territories are Glamoc, Kupres, Livno, Prozor, Tomislav Grad.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. This confirms that I was right when I said that Glamoc was included in Livno District. I've said that earlier. In the previous territorial arrangement, it was included in a territory with a majority Serb population.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Just one final question on this before we move on to the next topic. You were involved in these international negotiations, and help us out here. During those negotiations, did they ever pull out this decree and make this part of the negotiating process, and inform, say, Mr. Vance and Mr. Owen that this was, in fact, what the Presidency had decided and was, in fact, implementing at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina advised Mr. Vance and Mr. Owen of these contracts; but at the peace conference that I attended, these districts were not a subject of discussion. I don't know if the Presidency informed them of this, but these provinces, as they were accepted in the Vance-Owen Plan, we harmonised, we agreed at the meeting in Neum on the 22nd and 23rd of December, 1993, because it was 95 agreed -- 95 per cent agreed in conformity with the Vance-Owen maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. We're going to move on to the next topic, and this dealing primarily with the area I call it "April 1993." It's, for general purposes, sort of the topic for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And, first, I want to show P 01798, 1798.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And this is the 34th session held on 3 April 1993, the third session of the HVO. We see that your name is there being present; and, of course, we see from the very first item that Mr. Boban is there. And they're analysing the themes of the peace plan which had already been signed by the representatives of the Croatian and Muslim people in BH. So this is a month after the letter from the Ministry of Defence regarding the districts. Here, it would appear that we're back to the peace plan. And, of course, I want to focus your attention to the second-to-last paragraph on page 2, where it says, and this is part of a letter, as I understand it, or a letter to be sent, that: "Until the Republic is fully demilitarised, the armed forces will be organised in accordance with the relevant documents of the Vance-Owen Peace Plan, in accordance with the joint statement issued after the agreement by Mr. Boban," Mr. Mate Boban, "and Mr. Alija Izetbegovic, who led the delegations of the Croat and Muslims at the peace talks. "The statement was signed by Mr. Mate Boban, and its integral part reads as follows," and we don't need to read it. Now, having attended this meeting - and you don't need to go into any detail. If the Judges have questions, I'm sure they will ask - was it your understanding at the time that this was correct, that, in fact, Mr. Alija Izetbegovic and Mr. Boban had, indeed, signed an agreement concerning the Vance-Owen Peace Plan?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this session, Mr. Boban presented it this way in his introductory remarks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I'll move on to the next document, unless there are any questions from the Judges. 1D 02003.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This is dated 9 May 1993; and, here, we see that it says the HVO decided, at a meeting on 3 April 1993, that members of the HZ-HB HVO should visit all municipalities and provinces 3, 8, and 10 in order to familiarise the persons responsibility with the essence of the Vance-Owen documents and decisions made at the meeting of the HZ-HB HVO. And, of course, if we look at number 6, we see for Konjic, Jablanica, Prozor, and Rama, we see your name along with Mr. Kvesic, who I understand was with the Department of the Interior at the time. And my question is: Did you, indeed, go visit those areas as it reflects in this particular plan, May 9th?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm familiar with this plan, but I did not go with Mr. Kvesic to these municipalities, because very soon after this, I was to go visit Central Bosnia. I know, from the reports, that Mr. Kvesic did go.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you go to Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, let's look at 1D 02738.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And this is from "Vjesnik," dated 29 April 1993. Now, this predates the plan, and it says here, very first paragraph, this is Mostar: "The Vice-President of the Croatian Defence Council of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, Creso Zubak; the head of the Department for Justice and Administration, Zoran Buntic; and the head of the Under-Department of Labour, Social Welfare, and the Family, are on a two-day visit to the municipalities of Central Bosnia." So is this what you were telling about earlier, that you spent two days in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. This is a report about this trip to Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we go on to the next document, this may be of some interest both to you and the Trial Chamber, P02142, dated 29 April 1993, Citluk, where you hail from, as I understand it, and where you practice law. If we look on page 4 -- if we look on page 4, we see your name, and there you provide some commentary, some opinion; and we need to get from you some testimony concerning what exactly you're trying to say here, to ensure that the Trial Chamber understands from you and can perhaps ask you questions, as opposed to hearing theories from the parties. What are you saying here?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's obvious from this that this meeting was held a day or two after I returned from Central Bosnia, where I had been with this delegation visiting municipalities Vitez, Busovaca, Travnik, Kresevo, Kiseljak, and Zenica. We found that the situation was particularly difficult and grave in Zenica, where we had intended to visit the Zenica HVO; however, that was not possible. What was possible was to find the leadership of the HVO, Zenica, in St. Ilijas's Church in town, where we were received by Fra Stipan, the priest. And I have to emphasise that we arrived in Zenica on the SFOR armoured personnel carriers, practically secretly because it was the only possible means of travel there. And as we were entering the church, we were shielded by SFOR APCs; whereas, just outside the church, in the park, there were around 50 tents holding between 100 and 300 persons. And it was quite obvious that none of these persons were citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina, which was obvious from their appearance and their clothing. Inside, we found the president of Zenica HVO, who informed us that all of the Zenica HVO had been disarmed, and that they were all being locked up in some mine in Zenica. The people were crying for help because they were in a desperate and hopeless situation, and they also wanted advice, what to do. I remember very clearly that I said at that meeting what was the official political position of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, that they had to remain in that territory, after which the people asked me a very logical question: How? How were they to stay, and how we can defend them from what was outside in the park opposite the church? It was a fact that everyone in the HVO, Zenica, was disarmed and held imprisoned in some mine. So after I presented the official views, the president asked me, "Okay. That's your official view." In fact, the priest, Fra Stipe, asked me if I can give him my personal opinion, and I said, "No. I'm only authorised to give you the official position." After that, I went to a meeting in Citluk; and from the representatives who attended the meeting, I sought their opinion, what to do and how to proceed in these situations. How were we to help those people who were obviously seeking help and needed help? This segment that reflects what I said, I don't think it faithfully reflects my thoughts and what I said. It's obviously the phrasing chosen by the clerk who made the notes, but some of his formulations are clumsy and awkward and might lend themselves to misinterpretation. I mean, I can see that five sentences here begin with the words: "He thinks ... ," "He thinks ... ," so this is the understanding of the recording clerk, not what I actually said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: First of all, who are these people that you said were obviously not citizens of Bosnia-Herzegovina? You said "from their appearance." Perhaps you could tell us what they looked like, and perhaps you could tell us who they were, if you know.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was quite evident that those people come from the Middle East. It was obvious from their appearance with the small beards, the way they were dressed, the turbans, and all the rest, all different headgear. It was obvious they were not from Bosnia-Herzegovina, it was obvious they were not citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina, And all this was later confirmed by the president of the HVO and Father Stipe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, you say "the president of the HVO." That's the president of the local HVO?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. You are correct. The HVO, Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Let me put to you what is being alleged here. It's being alleged here that what you're representing, and others, during that time was reverse ethnic cleansing, to cleanse the Croats from Central Bosnia in order to repopulate them into Herzegovina, in order to make it more homogeneous than it already was. Was this -- are you suggesting that in this particular meeting, concretely?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, just for the Court's attention, I want to go back to a document. We'll have to flip back a little bit. It's 1D 01670, unless it was --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's your next document. We rearranged your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We saw this document yesterday or the day before, Your Honours, 1D 01670. And these are the minutes -- it was yesterday, in fact -- no. It was the day before. It's the 3 July 1992 minutes of the meeting of the Presidency. And as you may recall, I indicated that Mr. Buntic was responding to what a Mr. Blago Artukovic from Zenica said on 3 July 1992. Of course, the Citluk meeting is April 29, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So let's see, let's take a walk back in history, and see what Mr. Artukovic said to which you responded? On page 4 of the minutes -- Mr. Buntic, I believe it's the very next document in your binder. It's 1D 01670. On page 4, item 8, it says: "Blago Artukovic, Zenica: "Due to the prominent Muslim population in Zenica Municipality, the HVO organisation there was quite poor. The Muslims did not accept a single suggestion from the HVO. "He suggested that they be given political and military assistance. The situation was quite grave and the HVO numbered around 700 soldiers only. "The SDA and their leaders were advocating a unitary BH known as a civic one, and would not renounce that principle. The people were inadequately informed of the work and organisation of the HVO and HZ-HB." And, of course, then you respond to that. Naturally, he's speaking back on 3 July 1992. Would it be fair to say, Mr. Buntic, that when you went back there nearly a year, not quite a year later, that the situation was even more dangerous for the Croats as had been noted by Mr. Artukovic on 3 July 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As may be seen, there is a time difference here and the situation as it was when we were visiting Zenica. I described it. It was alarming and called for action. People's lives were at stake, and what Artukovic said at that time during that session obviously came true in the month of April 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We're going to move on to the next topic, and this deals with the implementation of the Vance-Owen Peace Plan. That's how I've titled it basically, so it doesn't necessarily mean that they were actually implementing anything. They were trying. If we look at now several documents in succession. Okay, the next document is 1D 01596.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This is the next chapter, the next area I'm going to, Mr. Buntic. Your documents have been organised in that fashion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So if you go into the next section, we're going to be looking at 1D 01596, 1597, 1598, 1599, 1600, 1601, and 1602. These are documents that we have seen. We've tendered them in the past, three times, and to no avail. They haven't been accepted yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But let me ask you this, Mr. Buntic: As a result of the Medjugorje agreement on May 18th, 1993, were you aware that Dr. Jadranko Prlic had been appointed to a position, which I believe was prime minister, as a result of that agreement?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was aware of that. Dr. Jadranko Prlic, himself, told us that. He was appointed the prime minister of a transitional government, in keeping with the Vance-Owen Plan. I'm familiar with Jadranko Prlic's documents proving his efforts to establish this transitional government.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... step by step. We're talking about prime minister for Bosnia-Herzegovina at the time, or what was envisaged out of Medjugorje. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that the proper term was a transitional government. He was the prime minister of this transitional government. I believe that that was its name. I'm also familiar with some other facts, because after that appointment, Mr. Jadranko Prlic did not chair two or three sessions of the HVO. It was his deputy, Mr. Kresimir Zubak, who chaired those sessions. And I remember that, maybe two or three sessions later, that he did not chair. When he arrived at one of the sequences sessions which was not held in Mostar, but in Siroki Brijeg, he was being joked about. There were jokes because -- and teased because the government had a lot more work than we had at the time. So we asked what he was doing there amongst us because the Vance-Owen Plan had to be implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Was it your understanding at the time that during the sessions that he missed, that he was working in his capacity -- in his newly-appointed capacity? Was that the understanding that you had, and others?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The way I understood it was that he was no longer the president of the HVO, because according to the agreement, he had been appointed the prime minister of the transitional government. And as I've just told you, I believe that government had a lot more work with regard to the implementation of the Vance-Owen Plan, which I thought was a major job that had to be carried out, and that he no longer was due to waste time at the HVO session because this other duty was more important.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. If we go on now to another set of documents. As I understand it, you've told us already that you had been in Geneva in January. Did you go back or did you participate in any other activities related to the implementation of the Vance-Owen Peace Plan? And, specifically, I'm referring to drafting legislation.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was in Geneva sometime between the end of May 1993 until the end of the first week of June 1993. The negotiations and the work that we did was carried out in the United Nations building in Geneva. The person in charge was Szasz, I believe was his name. He was an official of the United Nations, and Mr. Owen or Mr. Stoltenberg's secretary, who also worked in the administration of the United Nations. On the Croatian side, I was a member of the negotiations; and on the Bosniak side, it was Professor Kasim Trnka. Our task was to prepare and offer the draft proposals for documents that would serve for the implementation of the Vance-Owen Plan. For the seven or ten days that we stayed in Geneva, this is exactly what we did all that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very quickly, if we look at 1D 02314, 1D 02314, and we look at the bottom of the page, we see the name "Paul Szasz." I believe that's how to pronounce it. It appears to be a Hungarian name. I'm not sure. It's S-Z-A-S-Z. He's a legal adviser.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And would that be the gentleman that you're speaking of?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is indicated here he is the legal adviser of the United Nations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm going to have you look very quickly at documents, and I'm going to name them. And I would like you to flip through them briefly, and I'll ask you a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's 1D 02407, and this is a draft decree on the law establishing the provinces and their government bodies; 1D 02408, the draft decree law on the Ombudsman for the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina; 1D 02409, and this is a final text on the decree on the law on courts -- on the Court of Human Rights of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina; 1D 02410, draft decree on the adoption of international instruments for the protection of human rights in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina; 1D 02411, a draft decree law on cooperation with the International Monitoring Mission for Human Rights; 1D 02412, this is a decree on military counsel for the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina; and, lastly, 1D 02413, the decision to appoint members of the Military Consul of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Buntic, do you recognise these documents, and can you confirm to the Trial Chamber whether these are, indeed, the drafts that you had worked on while you were in Geneva, as was requested by Mr. Owen, working along with legal adviser for the UN, Mr. Szasz?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are the documents, and it is correct that I participated in the drafting, myself, together with Mr. Trnka. It is also correct that in the heading of these documents, at the top of these documents, you can see my handwriting, and I'm absolutely sure that this is my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, very briefly, before we leave this chapter: After these drafts were done in Geneva, can you please tell us what did you and others do concerning these drafts or any other matters related to the implementation of the Vance-Owen Peace Plan?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember very well that I did not go home from Geneva. I arrived at the Split Airport, where I was told to wait for the rest of the delegation at Split Airport. I was told that a flight had been scheduled for Sarajevo for further negotiations with the Bosniak side about the implementation and adoption of these documents that we had agreed upon in Geneva. The rest of the delegation from Mostar arrived at the airport. Members of the delegation were Mr. Boban, Mr. Prlic, Mr. Akmadzic, Mr. Petkovic, and maybe somebody else, but I'm not sure. And we were supposed to take off from Divulje in an UNPROFOR helicopter to Sarajevo to continue talks about the way the documents would be implemented and adopted by the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I know we got on two helicopters; and just before arriving in Sarajevo, the helicopter, which carried Mr. Boban, here present, General Petkovic, and I, was hit from an anti-aircraft machine-gun. The helicopter swayed and almost fell to the ground. The commander ordered us to return, and that's why we returned to Split. The helicopter was inspected, and that's when we learned that it had been hit seven times and that one of the bullets ended up some 12 centimetres from the tank. We asked the flight captain what would have happened if that had been the case, if it had ended up in the reservoir, and he said, "You wouldn't feel anything. You would be dead in two seconds or less." And whatever I'm saying here, I believe that it can be confirmed by General Petkovic. That was the story of the second helicopter. The first helicopter carried Mr. Prlic, Mr. Akmadzic, and maybe somebody else, but I can't remember at the moment. I can't remember who the third person was, if there was any.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... on your return, do you recall meeting anybody or having any discussions with anyone, formal or informal? You say you returned back to Split, to the air base.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we returned, they told us to stay put while the helicopter was being inspected to establish what had happened, because that is what was requested, and I know that a person talked to us. I remember that he was from Israel, but it's hard for me to remember his name after such a long time. I know that he represented a monitoring mission or some other international institution, but I really can't remember either his name or his position. The only thing that I'm sure of is that he was from Israel and that he was a member of the international forces or an international organisation, but I don't know what his position was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need to take a break. Yes, Mr. Karnavas, what did you want to add?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I just wanted to ask him about when this would have occurred, what was the month and the year when he took off from the UNPROFOR base in Divulje, flew in UNPROFOR, and, so, does he recall. Then that would be the end of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you recall the month and the year, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was June, and it was 1993. I'm sure of that. I'm not exactly sure about the date, but I believe it was the end of the first week of June or thereabouts. I know that we had been in Geneva from maybe the end of May to the beginning of June, but I know that I returned from Geneva in June. I didn't go home, so it must have been either the end of the first week or the beginning of the second week of June, or thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, when you say that you will be finished, does it mean that you've completed your examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I didn't say that, Your Honour. I said that we could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because I believe that you have about ten minutes left. The Registrar will tell us later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before I give the floor to Mr. Karnavas, we need two IC numbers for the photographs that were shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The map referring to the District of Mostar shall be given IC number 00826; while the second one, referring to Livno, shall be given Exhibit number IC 00827. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Karnavas, I believe you have 26 minutes left out of the seven hours you requested.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's correct. That's correct, Your Honour, and we just might be able to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Buntic, the next section deals with the Croatian Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna. I just need a confirmation, because we will have another witness go into greater detail. So I just want to cover three basic documents very quickly, and then we'll move on to the next two topics, which are a little bit more important.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The first document is P 04560, P 04560.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This is the 50th session of the HVO. And if we look at under item 2, 3, and 4 on page 3 in the English -- page 2 in the English document, we would see that your task, along with others, Mr. Zubak, Mr. Petkovic and others, is to draft the decision constituting the chamber, the deputies, the rules of procedure, and fundamental decisions? So do you recall and can you confirm for us that, indeed, not only were you tasked, but you, indeed, carried out those tasks?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I attended this session. It's correct this group was established, it's correct that I worked on the drafting of documents indicated here, and it's true that was the assignment given this group.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me. At least on my screen, the e-court doesn't appear to be working. I'm hoping that -- now it's working. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I hope you stopped the clock on that. Now, I feel it's overtime, Your Honour, and, you know, we're playing. 1D 01778. And along with this document, we're going to be looking at P 04611, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But if we look at first 1D 01778, we see that this is an agreement regarding Bosnia-Herzegovina. We see it's "Mostar, 1993," at the bottom. And, of course, we're going to be covering this in greater detail with another witness, particularly with respect to Roman numeral II and Roman numeral III in this document which deals with the constituent republics and their responsibilities the common institutions of the Union of Bosnia-Herzegovina. But just for confirmation purposes, can you please tell us what this agreement is, where did it come from, and how it was used? Just one sentence.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a draft agreement on the Stoltenberg plan, which was the immediate proposal of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna. It is a copy of a brochure, in fact, that was distributed at the time to all the MPs of the Parliament on the founding session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I asked -- well, let me ask you this way: Was this document used, this agreement and the contents there in, were they used by you or any others in your work in drafting any legislation that would have been part of the implementing process of the Owen-Stoltenberg Peace Plan?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. That's the agreement that serves the basis for the drafting of documents and the creation of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, if we look at P 04611, P 04611, we see that this is -- the first page is the preamble, rather long.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we go to the second page, we see this the basic decision on establishing and proclaiming the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna. So with leave from the Court, I will ask a leading question, which is: Was the document that we saw, the agreement, was this the basis for the drafting of the preamble in this particular basic decision?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I've already answered this question, saying that this agreement was especially important and it was the motive why we have opted for these arrangements.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We're going to go on to the next topic, and we need the usher's assistance. The next one I've titled: "Reports," and hopefully it will become obvious. If we look at 1D 02370, 1D 02370, that's the first document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And from here, it's a Department for Justice and General Administration, Mostar; and if we look through this document -- first of all, do you recognise the document?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a report of the Higher Court for Misdemeanors, which was hereby submitted to the General Administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And unless there are any questions from the Bench, I will move on to the next document. I think it's rather self-explanatory that the document contains certain observations, including problems. All right. Seeing no --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Go ahead. If you wish to say something, be brief, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps I'd like to draw your attention to two issues here in para 7. We see that misdemeanor courts, too, emphasised the problem of the payment system not working, and the other problem is the legislative bodies, due to inflation, do not determine fines quickly enough. And this is hereby confirmed by reports from the courts, themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. If we go on to the next document, 1D 01978, 1978, well, this is a report on the District Military Court until 30 June 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And, here, from the very first paragraph, we see that it's broken down to first quarter and second quarter. And if we look at the last sentence in the first page in English, that is, it says: "The basic prerequisite for the court to work successfully is unity. During the previous period, there was no unity in the District Military Court in Mostar." It then goes on to say: "The circumstances were such that there were two military factions, the HDZ -- HB-HZ and the former BH. This resulted in an absurd situation where part of the Court implemented the general policy of the other political authorities, which is contrary to the one which established the Court." Then it goes on to say: "For example, during the period in question, not a single session of a full bench of judges was held, which is also the result of obstruction of the work of the Court." Now, I recognise that your department was in charge of civilian courts, but can you comment on this particular document and what is being said here? And, again, this is for -- the purpose of this chapter of our direct is to demonstrate transparency and reporting.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. This is a report of the District Military Court, which was supposed to submit its reports to both the Department for Defence and the Department for Justice and General Administration. I would like to point out the reasons for my statement, the statement that I made perhaps an hour ago, saying that I assumed the responsibility for the work of all the judges in the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, but do not take responsibility for the work of judges appointed by the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And now I will tell you why. The reason why is that these judges appeared in court only once a month when it was pay day, and we see that from this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we go on to the next document, 1D020004, dated 6 August 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If you look at the very last page, we see your name, head of the department, "Zoran Buntic." And just can you confirm that this is your report? And, of course, there may be some things that the Court may wish to question you about. We see, for instance, in the second paragraph, that reports of the District Military Prosecutor's Office and District Military Courts are submitted to the head of the Defence Department at the same interval, and then from the head of the Defence Department to the Presidency or the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna? Perhaps you can comment on that a little bit. I mean, what was the purpose of it, if you know? Then I would ask you also to look at item 13 on page 3, where it says: "Certain commanders of civilian and military police, those who deal with requests which have not been made by the HVO or of the HZ-HB, do not act in line with decisions of civilian and military courts, but simply ignore them. "We want all those responsibility to warn that legally-valid decisions are not to be discussed, but observed." If you could comment on that, please, very briefly.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. This is my report, the one that I wrote personally. I don't know why my signature is not here, but it is my report and I stand by it. I stand by every word of it. I was trying to draw the attention, through this report, that reports should be submitted as prescribed by the valid regulations of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna; and, somehow, people automatically submitted them to the Department for Justice and General Administration. I personally stand by every word in this report. I wrote it myself. I don't know why the signature is missing, but it's not logical that this document was not signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, I'm going to go through a series of reports. I'm just going to read out the numbers, and you have them in chronological order. So you just have to look at them, and I'm going to ask you whether you can confirm these reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Karnavas. This previous document, it's rather interesting, in particular the number 13 you have drawn attention to, which seems to indicate that it was difficult to implement the law, to have the law respected. And I would like to ask you, Witness: Did you take any further steps in order to change this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a report dated for the 1st of January, 1993, until the 6th of August, 1993. As you know, immediately after this report, I left the position of chief of Department for Justice and General Administration, as you know. On the 28th of August, 1993, the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna was established, and I was no longer a minister of justice there. I was in that position before Herceg-Bosna was set up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Buntic. Now, I'm going to read several numbers out, and I'll go through them rather slowly, and ask you whether you can confirm that these are reports. Again, this is in order for the Trial Chamber to see what was happening and to take notice of the transparency.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: 1D 01974, this is dated 5 August, 1993; 1D 02015, again, this is from Livno, 5 August 1993; 1D 02005, we see your name at the bottom; 1D 02341, this is 26 August 1993; 1D 02378, 27 August 1993; 1D 02377, 8 October 1993; 1D 02376, this is 9 October 1993; 1D 02369, 11 October 1993; 1D 02375, this is a report from 1 January 1993 to 30 September 1993; 1D 02374, again, from 1 January to 30 September 1993; 1D 02368, 12 October 1993; 1D 01777, this is 19 October 1993; 1D 01797, 8 November 1993; 1D 02285, and we see that this is 26 November 1993; and, finally, 1D 01976, and this is a report from July to November 1993. I'm sorry. There's one more document: 1D 02372, 16 December 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, I do understand from your previous answer that you would not have been -- you did not occupy the position as the head of the department; however, you were familiar with the reporting process, and as I understand it, you have looked through these documents. Can you confirm to the Trial Chamber that these documents represent the sort of reporting that was ongoing at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously, these are reports of the work of judiciary bodies, courts, prosecutors' offices, misdemeanor courts, in the territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna for the period indicated; but as I said, all these reports were also submitted to the Department for Justice and General Administration. And until the 28th of August, they were submitted to the Department for Justice and General Administration, and, afterwards, to the Ministry of Justice. Until August, I received them; but after that date, the 28th of August, they were received by the Minister of Justice of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which was later Mr. Zubak. Yes, those are the reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me. Counsel, I apologise for the interruption, and, Mr. President, I'm going to lodge an objection. If you want to take it against the Prosecution's time for cross, that's okay. But I want to raise at this point, once upon a time, a witness by the name of Christopher Beese as a Prosecution witness. The Prosecution attempted to tender through Mr. Beese, who was with the ECMM, a large number of ECMM documents that he had reviewed ahead of time and was indicating were all appropriate reports of the ECMM. The Prosecution was not permitted to tender the documents of the ECMM through him in that way. I think that's essentially what is now happening here. And I recognise that counsel's under time limitations, but I think it's worth noting for the record, and we will raise this in our written response to whatever documents are tendered by Mr. Karnavas, but I think that what's happening here is the very same process that the Prosecution was denied using with Mr. Beese on the ECMM documents. So I just note that objection for the record. And if you want to assign the time for my objection to my cross, I'm okay with that. I don't want to cut Mr. Karnavas off or limit his time, but I just wanted to raise it for the record at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll respond, Mr. President, when we see their written submissions on this, but again I wanted to note that the purpose -- one of the primary purposes was to demonstrate the reporting that was ongoing for transparency purposes. But we take Mr. Stringer's observations to heart. We look forward to his written submissions, and we will respond accordingly. And we welcome that intervention because we do recognise he has the need to make a record, as we do. 1D 01676 is the next document -- 75. I'm sorry, 1675.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Here, this is dated 18 August 1993, and we can see that this is a working meeting. We see that you are named there, so you would have been present. And, of course, we see that your department -- well, what's interesting is paragraph 3 and paragraph number 6. But then if we look at Roman numeral II, it talks about analysis of the application of criminal sanctions established, and that: "In some areas criminal sanctions are not being put into effect, although valid and excusable and executable court decisions exist. In other areas, the circumstances for their application are nonexistent; and, thus, not only is the purpose of punishment not accomplished, but the result is also utter distrust in the organs of authority and a rise of the feelings of insecurity among the citizens. Concerning this matter, the meeting established the following conclusions," and we can see certain conclusions. Can you verify, sir, whether, indeed, you were at this particular meeting? And I suspect you might have also contributed to the analysis that I just read and to the conclusion that are reached, that are contained herein.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you can see from the header and from the introductory part of the record, I did attend and did participate in the work of this session. I have the minutes here from the 18th of August. You said "8th August." I don't know if we mean the same record. I have minutes of the 18th of August. It's true that I attended that meeting where these topics were discussed, and I believe the conclusions, as phrased here, correctly reflect the conclusions of that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: One last document in this area, and that's 1D 01813, 1813.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This is dated 18 September 1993, and we see that this is a letter to the supreme commander of the armed forces of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna and to the president of the Chamber of Deputies of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna; and it's by Dr. Jadranko Prlic, president of the government of the HR-HB. And if we look at the very first paragraph, it says that: "In the analysis of the application of the law in the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna made several months ago, the Government of HR-HB stated that all forms of unlawfulness had increased, especially crime. It has, therefore, adopted the appropriate measures and activities to prevent and combat this." And I'm wondering whether you might able to provide some assistance of whether you were aware of the problems that are being discussed and the solutions that are being proposed in this particular document.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's obviously an enactment, a document that was made after this session, the same day when the session was held on the 18th of August, 1993. And as far as I know, this was followed, I think, by Action Pauk, Spider, an action to combat crime in the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, which was soon to be replaced by the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm told the date is wrong. It says 18th September --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You indicated that it was 18 August; and from the document, it's 18 September. So did you misspeak or are we to take it that the meeting was actually on the 18th of August?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. That meeting was held on the 18th of August, and this document, yes, right says 18th September. The document is of the 18th of September, one month later, already at the time when the Republic -- Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna was created.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm sorry. Witness, on the last paragraph of the first page, this document refers to a meeting of 17 September 1993, not "a month ago."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know if we have the same documents before us. Under 1D 01675, I have minutes from a working meeting held on the 18th August, 18 August 1993; and that is the document that I have under the number I just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I, Witness, am looking at document 1D 01813. I was of the opinion that that was the one counsel has actually put before us; 1D 01813, dated 18 September 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's a different document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: No. Your document is different, Witness. This is the document. You seem to be looking at the wrong document, and I ask you to look at the right one. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Maybe I can clarify it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Buntic, let's move to the last document in this chapter, and that is 1D 01813. Mr. Prlic has written to the Supreme Command, the supreme commander of the Armed Forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina, as well as to the president of Chamber of Deputies. He's referring to a situation that obviously has been building up, because he has indicated that in an analysis of the application of the laws of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna made "several months ago" - and we know that up until August sometime, you were in the Department of Justice - the government of the HR-HB stated that all forms of unlawfulness had increased, especially crime. It has, therefore, adopted the appropriate measures and activities. Now, can you comment on this, on this particular document itself, and do you know whether any actions were taken as a result of this particular letter by Dr. Jadranko Prlic, who at the time was serving as president of the government, and this must have been a decision that the government took?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I stopped working in the HZ-HB and when the HZ-HB stopped existing, I think that this document is the implementation of the conclusions that were reached at the meeting on the 18th of August, 1993. As far as I know, after this document, an action was launched to fight crime, and its name was Pauk or Spider. And I believe this document is in this regard, and that's the only thing I can say because as of that time I was no longer involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's go to the very last topic, and that's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Mr. Buntic, you were not in office anymore when this letter was written. I wonder what you know about this letter and about the proposal to have a meeting concerning the crime problem. How do you know about it when you were not in office anymore at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have told you the truth. I was at the meeting on the 18th of August, 1993. We're talking about the previous document, number 1D 01675. Obviously, at that session, certain conclusions were reached. I've also stated that the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna became the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna on the 28th of August, 1993, and that I was no longer in any position. But I believe that this document, dated 18 September, was part of the implementation of the conclusions which were adopted at the session on the 18th of August, 1993, and I've also said that I believe - I'm not sure, therefore, but I know how I would in my answer - that after this document, an action was launched under the title "Pauk" to fight crime, which was then to be implemented for the next six or seven months. But I said it with a caveat that I wasn't sure, that I believed it was in regards to the conclusions of that session, and that the Action Pauk ensued. But I'm not sure of those facts. I just believe that that was the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, there are two or three minutes remaining.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. I think it will be a topic that will pique everyone's interests, including members of the Bench. So I'm sure the questions that I don't ask, the Bench might wish to ask. This deals with the issue of prisons. If we look at - and specifically, Your Honours, just in case I'm cut off - the documents that I would like to go through with the gentleman are P 00452, 1D 01105, 1D 02826, 1D 02384, P 03350, P 02679, P 03560, P 03573, 1D 02909. So these are the documents. I put them on the record, because especially I heard a rather interesting observation from Judge Prandler where he indicated why we didn't bring the Constitution and so on, and I just wanted to demonstrate through this. Again, it's impossible, with the time constraints, to do everything, but I don't want to leave the impression that we're shying away from a particular area, which then calls into question my credibility as an advocate for my client or the credibility of the witness. So there is no intention or we're not trying to hide. We're just trying to make due with the time that we have. So if we look at P 00452 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, Mr. Karnavas. My colleague has pointed out that we all agree, but if you feel that the issues are important, since you're master of your own time credit, you can take additional time that we deducted from your time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll do that, I'll do that. I recognise I only have so many chips to play, you know, and I have to make some decisions. On this hand, I'll play as many as I can. If we look at P 00452, this is a decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It says here that: "The Central Military Prison of the HZ-HB is hereby established at the Mostar-Jesenica location, within the Heliodrom barracks." Now, can you tell me us if you know anything about this, because obviously your department to some extent was or would have been involved, it would appear from what we saw a couple of days ago.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try and be brief. At the end of the first day of my testimony, I said that upon taking over my duties, I had spoken with the president of the Higher Court in Mostar, who was in charge of the situation in the District Investigation Prison in Mostar. That was the only institution of that kind which we had in the entire territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. The president of that court informed me at the time that in addition to the prisoners who were serving various sentences, there were also prisoners of war there. Shortly after that, I sent a letter, i.e., I sent a proposal to the Defence Department, giving them my reasons why civilians and military personnel cannot share the same facility, and I meant ordinary prisoners and prisoners of war. We also spoke about a decree, how locations would be chosen where detained persons would be kept. Immediately after that, the Defence Department, as we can see here already on the 3rd of September, issued a decision to establish the Central Military Prison for the entire territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. And as it is indicated here, it was established in Mostar, in the area called Jesenica, which was a former barracks of the JNA, also known as Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I think that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We'll go on to the next document, 1D 01045.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Here, we have a decision granting permission to the Misdemeanor Prison and the detention facility in the Capljina barracks to higher certain employees. And we see, if we look at the bottom of it, this is the president of the Croatian Defence Council, Pero Margetic. And as I understand, he was the president of the HVO for Capljina. Can you please explain how is it that he's making this decision.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One correction. It is not Pero Margetic but Pero Markovic. It is true that he was the president of the Municipal Board of Capljina, and this is a misdemeanor prison. It was the municipal organs that were authorised in the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: 1D 02836, this is dated 16 March 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We see you at the bottom of the page, your name; and this is a request for the delivery of uniforms for Mostar District Prison Services. And, of course, we see that you're writing to the Republic of Croatia, the Ministry of Justice. And I have two questions: One, why did you write to the Republic of Croatia; and, two, more importantly, did you have any contact, that is, personal contact, with representatives of the Republic of Croatia concerning this or any other matter related to the establishment or the functioning of this or other prisons which you were responsible for?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it was immediately before this day that the decision was passed at a HVO session about the appearance of the uniforms for the army, for the police, and the judicial police, since at the time we did not have the money to create our own uniforms. What we adopted was the appearance of uniforms such as existed in the Republic of Croatia. The style and the colour was the same as in the Republic of Croatia, and I just told you why. We did not have any money to come up with some new solutions for uniforms, and this looked like a very practical solution. And that's why this request was sent to the Minister of Justice in the General Administration of the Republic of Croatia, with a request for their assistance. We requested them to send us uniforms for the judicial police. It is true that I signed those documents. And as for your second question, I will answer by saying this: Never, during my term of office, did I meet with the Minister of Justice of the Republic of Croatia. Even later on, when I was the president of the Judicial Council of the Republic of Croatia, I never met with the president of the Judicial Council of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we look at the next document, 1D 02384, 1D 02384, this is nominations for prison wardens.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And we see, at the bottom, this is the assistant to the head of the HZ-HB Justice Department, Mato Tadic, who I understand it currently sits on the Constitutional Court in Bosnia-Herzegovina and has been -- has held Ministry positions since the Dayton Peace Accord. Can you please explain who Tadic, Mato Tadic, was at the time, whether you had any working relationship with him, and how is it that it is he that is making the nominations for the prison wardens? And this is for a military and civilian prison to be established in Bosanski Brod, Orasje District. Be very brief about it, please.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that this is about Mr. Tadic, who was my assistant, indeed, all the time he was in Bosanska Posavina. It was very difficult or impossible for us to communicate, for the well-known reasons, but this is not about him appointing anybody. It is obvious that he submits a proposal for the prison warden to be appointed, and this proposal was sent to the HQ of the HZ-HB for Bosanska Posavina, i.e., Orasje to be more precise, because at that time, we could not establish physical communication. That was in March 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you confirm that he currently sits on the Constitutional Court in BiH, or do I have it wrong?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. And before that, he was the Minister of Justice of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we look at the next document, P 03350, this is a work report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's dated for the period of 1 January 1993 to 31 June 1993. Very transparent. We see your name at the bottom of the last page. And, of course, the Judges may wish to ask questions, although I would kindly ask that the questions be asked tomorrow, so I can finish up, myself. But you will notice that on item number 11, which is on page 3 in English, it talks about the Capljina prison has been relocated to Gabela and its warden appointed. And then on number 12, it talks about the Mostar District Prison is not functioning, so the prisoners have been relocated to the Heliodrom. And, of course, the Trial Chamber may wish to ask about number 13. I'm not going to ask, due to my time limitations. But could you please explain to us, on number 11, the Capljina prison having been relocated to Gabela, what are we talking about here?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In one of the previous documents with regard to the same subject, we saw that the Municipality of Capljina adopted a decision on establishing a misdemeanor prison in the Capljina barracks. As I already said, municipalities had full authority both for the establishment of prisons as well as for their functioning and the work of misdemeanor courts. They were also authorised; and in keeping with the law, they could, indeed, issue decisions on the establishment of misdemeanor prisons. Document number 1D 01105, i.e., this particular decision that we're looking at, shows that the Municipality of Capljina did exactly that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. That was my next question, but I'm glad you anticipated it. And, again, I know the Judges may have questions on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm told that I need to repeat the number. That was 1D 01105. That was the document that we saw earlier, Your Honours, and that's the document that Mr. Buntic was referring to, confirming what he had said earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And, again, thank you for anticipating my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm going to move on to the next document, P 02679, and this is a decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's dated June 8, 1993. We see that it's signed by Dr. Jadranko Prlic on behalf of the HVO. It's a decision made by the HVO. And it says here that the county military prison and the county prison for the areas of Capljina, Neum, Ljubuski, and Rama municipalities is hereby being set up in Gabela.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And before I ask my question, I wish to point to everyone's attention the preamble, which makes reference to Article 145, paragraph 2 of the Law on Implementing Criminal Procedure of the Misdemeanor Sanctions. And, of course, for Your Honours and for everyone else's information, that would be 1D 02909. That's where you would find Article 145.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very briefly, did you participate in the meeting or -- you know, the HVO meetings that took place in passing this particular decision, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that the HVO issued this decision. Also, I don't remember that this decision was ever published in the Official Gazette of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. I did not see this decision before. The first time I seen it was here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we go on to the next document, P 03560, this is minutes of the 46th session of the HVO, 19 July 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We see that you're present in that particular session, and then we can look at the conclusions in that. And, of course, under item 7, on page 4, before conclusions, we see after item 7 says: "After discussion of the request of the HVO at the Capljina Municipality to relocate prisoners in a discussion on the status and accommodation conditions of prisoners and persons in isolations, with the aim of improving their accommodation conditions and overcoming the newly-arisen situation, unanimous approval was given in adopting the following," and then we go to and we see the part of the conclusions to secure accommodation conditions relative -- you know, that are in accordance with the Geneva Conventions. And, of course, we see that you are part of a working group, under item 2. And, of course, a deadline is being given of the following day, 20 July 1993. Could you please comment on this? Obviously, you must have been present. You were tasked. What was this about, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As may be seen from the minutes, this is a request by the Municipality of Capljina to relocate quite a large number of prisoners who were in the territory of Capljina that moment, due to the bad conditions that prevailed in the places where those people were detained. It is true that by conclusion of the government, a group was assigned, consisting of Zoran Buntic, Darinko Tadic, and Berislav Pusic. It is also true that on that same day or maybe the following day, we visited the Municipality of Capljina, as had been provided for by the conclusion. And we spoke about the problems that they had emphasised in the request, and that was discussed at the government session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And if we then look at P0 3573, we see that these are minutes of the 47th session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's dated July 20th. That would be the deadline that was given the previous day. We see that you are, indeed, present, and I assume you've looked at this document. And would it be fair to say that it was on this date that you gave a report based on your -- the observations that you had been tasked with?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN BUNTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As it is stated here in the minutes, on that same day or on the following day, we submitted our report to the HVO about our visit to the Municipality of Capljina, and we also had certain proposals for them, for the HVO. This group carried out the task given to it by the HVO. We visited Capljina, and, on the following day, we submitted our report about that visit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Buntic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That concludes my direct examination. That was a little shorter on this particular topic, but I believe Your Honours may wish to ask some questions based on the answers that we just received. Again, thank you, sir, and I trust you will be as forthright with the Prosecution and anyone else who asks you questions over the course of the next few days. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stringer, 30 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution would be grateful to have some idea from the other Defence teams how much time they have in mind to use during their own examinations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very briefly, D2.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, D2 intends to submit their request for additional time, because on direct, some topics were touched upon that are of some importance for the Defence of Mr. Stojic, in terms of reporting prisons, military judiciary, and judiciary, and especially the establishment of Heliodrom that the witness mainly outlined in his testimony. But these are very important issues, and the time allocated to me will be too short. And based on the documents that we are going to submit, we will be able to judge whether you can allocate us additional time for our examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But how much time will you need, Ms. Nozica, how much time?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in the distribution of time, since you're asking me first and I can only talk about my time, I've been allocated 30 minutes, and I need an additional one hour. And I am prepared to deduct that from my total time because I believe it is important to clarify some issues with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Praljak's Defence will need about 15 minutes for cross-examination, not more. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, according to my calculations, we should be allocated 50 per cent of the time that was spent on direct examination, which is a little bit more than my learned friend Nozica calculated as particular times for particular Defence teams. In my view, we are entitled to 42 minutes or thereabouts, and I'm going to submit my request for additional time of one hour and a half. Tomorrow, you will be able to see whether the topics that I need to discuss with the witness are relevant or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC-TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. My situation is largely dependent on the technical situation. If we have 42 minutes, as my learned friend Alaburic has stated, I'm grateful; and if I were to show all the CDs and if I were able to have the technical support, then I would be able to finish within that time or maybe a couple of minutes more than that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D6?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pusic's Defence will take no longer than 15 minutes. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. We'll let you know what we decide tomorrow. We have to stop here because there's another trial after us. See you tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 10th day of July, 2008, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.48 p.m.,
